summaries.title: Autophagy
summaries.summary: The material indicates that autophagy signalling is altered in CTEPH pulmonary vasculature, although the direction of change differs between human lesions and animal models. In pulmonary artery lesions from CTEPH patients, the autophagy markers BECN1 (beclin-1) and LC3 were elevated alongside increased collagen deposition, defining a TGF-β/Smad3-LC3 axis as a driver of disease and a target for pharmacological modulation of autophagy, for example with riociguat [41912928, PPR1079116]. In contrast, a rat CTEPH model showed decreased Beclin-1 and LC3B with increased tissue factor expression, suggesting LC3B may be protective by regulating endothelial cell proliferation during CTEPH pathogenesis [27234007]. Autophagy-related gene ATG7 is regulated by non-coding RNAs: overexpressed miR-382-3p promotes vascular remodelling via ATG7 inhibition [37608664], and the lncRNA APF/miR-188-3p/ATG7 axis was examined in paired CTEPH vascular specimens [42491119]. PDGF transiently phosphorylated Akt, mTOR and p70S6 kinase in CTEPH cells, implicating mTOR in pulmonary vascular remodelling and suggesting benefit from rapamycin [19633069], though basal mTOR levels versus control cells remain unconfirmed [33692478]. A role for PIK3C3 (VPS34) in promoting thrombosis in CTEPH is suggested but not established [39821606].

summaries.title: Cell Cycle
summaries.summary: Several cell-cycle-associated genes are implicated in CTEPH, largely through proliferative vascular remodelling and clonal haematopoiesis. Network analyses of CTEPH tissue place TP53 and MYC among the most highly connected hub proteins across cell types, with circ_0007400 proposed to regulate TP53 as a competing endogenous RNA [36440052]. Non-coding RNA circuits also converge on cell-cycle control, as the hsa_circ_0002062–hsa-miR-942-5p–CDK6 pathway has been linked to CTEPH occurrence and development [31593832, 35229989], while miR-382-3p overexpression promotes pulmonary artery wall thickening with increased PCNA and VEGF expression via ATG7 inhibition [37608664]. Proliferative signalling involves ERK1/2 (MAPK3)-dependent migration of CTEPH pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells driven by the renin-angiotensin system [29122755], thrombin-activated Akt signalling [34736457], PI3K/Akt downstream of hsa-miR-122-5p–PIK3CG [41560055], and PRKCA-linked pathways [28904974]. Clonal haematopoiesis mutations, including STAG2, are enriched in CTEPH [PPR661171], and PAFAH1B1 is upregulated in CTEPH vascular samples [27124368, 33083107]. Transcriptional regulators EP300 [38451963, 39192976] and JAK2 V617F [33024690, 36949868] are additionally reported.

summaries.title: Cell-Cell communication
summaries.summary: The material depicts CTEPH as involving disturbed communication between vascular cells, immune cells and platelets. In pulmonary endarterectomy tissue, cells co-expressing the endothelial marker CD31 and α-SMA (ACTA1) indicate "intermediate" endothelial-to-muscle phenotypes in neointimal lesions, while α-SMA expression is lower in CTEPH pulmonary artery tissue than in donors and only a minority of neointimal α-SMA-positive cells express desmin or SMMHC [21854648, 22452949]; CDH5 was identified as the key molecular target linking particulate exposure to CTEPH [40188413, PPR899102]. Endothelial cells from PEA specimens show NF-κB (NFKB1) activation sustaining a pro-inflammatory state, which PRDX2 overexpression attenuates [33810533, 41372353]. Inflammatory mediators and signaling are prognostically and mechanistically relevant: IL-6 with sST2 predicts outcome [41571319] though T cell IL-6 does not separate patients from controls [35572511], STAT3 is upregulated in CD4+ Treg clusters [40567587], and JAK1/2 inhibition reduces vascular remodeling in rats [36555286, 39684570]. Platelet GTP-bound Rac1 and related GTPases were measured as activation markers [25169936, 36984870], and PKM2 is elevated in serum and PEA tissue, modulating endothelial mitochondrial metabolism and intimal remodeling [39360158, 41811700].

summaries.title: Cellular responses to stimuli
summaries.summary: The material depicts CTEPH as a disease in which pulmonary vascular cells mount sustained responses to inflammatory, oxidative and hypoxic stimuli. Inflammatory mediators are consistently elevated: CCL2 (MCP-1), proposed to be upregulated by blood pressure or shear stress as well as immune reactions, is higher in CTEPH patients than controls [26667361, 11463608]; CXCL8 is increased in plasma, correlates with survival and is expressed more highly in CTEPH than in IPAH [33947407, 38451963]; and IL6, together with sST2, is an independent prognostic biomarker in medically treated CTEPH, although intracellular T cell IL-6 does not distinguish patients from controls [41571319, 35572511]. Stress-response and redox genes are also altered, with increased PRDX2, whose overexpression limits inflammation via NF-κB signalling and modulates mitophagy to attenuate vascular remodelling [41372353], raised HMOX1 [39730379], and HSP70 (HSPA1A) failure supporting endothelial dysfunction [33270690]. Hypoxic signalling is shifted, with increased HIF-1α, decreased eNOS (NOS3) and downregulated HIF1α-AS1 [39823269, 37063122, 36323673]. Additional changes involve EGF, EZH2, APOA1 and albumin [35053115, 33313943, 33996028, 40941614].

summaries.title: Chromatin organization
summaries.summary: The material links chromatin-modifying and transcription-regulating genes to CTEPH. EZH2 expression was measured, at both protein and mRNA level, in pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells from CTEPH patients, implicating this histone-modifying enzyme in the diseased vascular wall [33313943]. EP300 was identified among genes with diagnostic and therapeutic value in CTEPH, particularly in chronic thrombosis, although unlike the co-identified inflammatory genes it was expressed lower in CTEPH than in idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension [38451963]; separately, EP300-regulated gene programmes, along with those of FLI-1 and ESRRA, were upregulated in CD16+ monocytes of CTEPH patients [39192976]. Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential mutations are enriched in CTEPH patients, with DNMT3A among the most frequently mutated genes [PPR661171]. Transcriptional inflammatory signalling is also implicated: phospho-NF-κB-P65 was detected in CTEPH endothelial cells and thrombus vessels [33810533], NF-κB activity was modulated by PRDX2 and by inhibitor treatment [41372353], and JAK2 V617F-mutant essential thrombocythaemia co-occurred with CTEPH [33024690, 36949868].

summaries.title: Circadian clock
summaries.summary: Several circadian clock-annotated genes appear in CTEPH through neurohormonal, transcriptional, fibrinolytic and metabolic mechanisms. The AVP-derived peptide copeptin, alongside MR-proANP, MR-proADM and CT-proET-1, has been measured prospectively in PAH and CTEPH cohorts to assess haemodynamics, exercise capacity and prognosis, and is altered in CTEPH, falling after therapy, with median levels comparable to those reported in mixed pulmonary hypertension cohorts [33263045, 26363916]. The transcriptional coactivator EP300 is proposed to have diagnostic and therapeutic value in chronic thrombosis, being expressed lower in CTEPH than in IPAH, while EP300-regulated genes are upregulated in CD16+ monocytes of CTEPH patients [38451963, 39192976]. For SERPINE1, PAI-1 complexes circulating t-PA, yet neither high resting PAI-1 activity nor blunted t-PA release explains CTEPH; a PAI-1 polymorphism has been examined as a genetic determinant [1394930, 41596405]. PPARGC1A (PGC-1alpha) with mtTFA mediates PKM2-dependent endothelial mitochondrial metabolism and intimal remodelling [41811700], PPARA agonists reduce TAFIalpha [40588471], PPAR-linked fatty-acid metabolism and CD36 are implicated [32110389], MEF2D links miR-665 to smooth-muscle proliferation [32699607], and PPP1CA discriminates CTEPH from FM-PH [41827036].

summaries.title: DNA Repair
summaries.summary: The material links three DNA repair-associated genes to CTEPH, although the evidence reported concerns vascular remodelling and inflammation rather than DNA repair function itself. In protein-protein interaction networks built from different pulmonary cell types, TP53 was among the genes with the highest connectivity, suggesting a hub role in CTEPH progression [36440052]. TP53 was also proposed to be regulated by circ_0007400 acting as a competing endogenous RNA in cancer stem cells and CRISPLD2+ cells, providing a possible mechanism for its involvement [36440052]. PARP-1 levels were significantly upregulated in patients with CTEPH, as well as in IPAH and COPD-PH, compared with controls (p < .0001) [34190625]. In a rat model, CTEPH increased PCNA expression together with VEGF and autophagy-related proteins; a miR-382-3p antagomir reversed these changes and the associated mPAP elevation and pulmonary artery wall thickening, whereas a miR-382-3p agomir potentiated them, implicating miR-382-3p-driven, ATG7-dependent vascular remodelling [37608664].

summaries.title: Developmental Biology
summaries.summary: The material frames CTEPH as a disease in which developmental/growth-factor signalling drives thrombus non-resolution and vascular remodelling. Endothelin-1 and TGF-β are described as pivotal in CTEPH pathophysiology and vascular remodelling, with circulating levels assessed before and after pulmonary endarterectomy [39274190], the ET-1 pathway implicated in CTEPH microvasculopathy [39550495], and defective endothelial TGF-β signalling tested for its contribution to thrombus non-resolution and fibrosis using platelet TGFB1 and endothelial TGFβRII deletions [31747868]. Systemic EGF was elevated in CTEPH but not iPAH [35053115], while EZH2 was measured in CTEPH pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells [33313943] and FOXO1 was linked to apoptosis and autophagy during pulmonary artery remodelling [28536427, PPR689684]. Matrix remodelling involves MMP2, reportedly upregulated through loss of miR-106b-5p [32699607] and by ginsenoside Rg1 [23738715]. These programmes act alongside inflammation, including TNF, CCL2, IL1B, CXCL8 and IL6 and CD14+/CD16+ monocyte-macrophage responses [26667361, 11463608, 32741891, 39192976, 38451963, 33947407, 35572511, 41571319].

summaries.title: Disease
summaries.summary: The material depicts CTEPH as a disease involving coagulation, inflammation and vascular remodelling mechanisms. Coagulation abnormalities include decreased ADAMTS13 with increased VWF levels in CTEPH compared with healthy controls, implicating the ADAMTS13–VWF axis in CTEPH pathobiology [30655285], with elevated FVIII and VWF:Ag not explained by VWF or F8 mutations [41300788]; ADAMTS13 levels in CTEPH are higher than in pulmonary arterial hypertension [34616545], and heparin-calibrated anti-Xa measurement informs treatment of CTEPH patients receiving FXa inhibitors [39468095, PPR925396]. Inflammatory mechanisms include increased CCR6+ CD4+ T cells at diagnosis and in vascular lesions [35572511], recruitment of CD16+ monocytes to pulmonary artery intima and differentiation into IL-1β-high macrophages [39192976], higher IL1B and other chemokine/cytokine gene expression than in IPAH [38451963], raised serum HMGB1 [25188497, 36314346], and increased PRDX2, whose overexpression attenuates inflammation via NF-κB and alleviates vascular remodelling [41372353]. Additional reported factors are the heterozygous RNF213 p.Arg4810Lys variant in 7.1% of patients, affecting balloon pulmonary angioplasty response [39056331, 40240930], dysfunctional ApoA-I [33996028], elevated ADAMTSL4 [37448441], HGF [30594174] and ANO1 polymorphisms [42346503].

summaries.title: Drug ADME
summaries.summary: The material links CTEPH to proteins that govern drug absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion, although most evidence is indirect. Serum albumin, the principal plasma drug-binding protein, was inversely correlated with length of stay in CTEPH and strongly predicted prolonged hospitalisation and mortality (AUC = 0.833), and was also evaluated as part of the NT-proBNP-to-albumin ratio (NTAR) alongside the RDW-to-eGFR ratio (RGR) [40941614, 41515551]. Paraoxonase-1 enzymatic activity was measured with HDL-C, ApoA-I and oxidised dysfunctional oxTrp72-ApoA-I in CTEPH patients versus healthy controls, the first such assessment of ApoA-I derangement in CTEPH [33996028]. CYP2C9*3 and CYP2C9*7 polymorphisms were genotyped in Turkish CTEPH patients but showed no association with disease, unlike the fibrinogen-Aα THR312ALA variant [36856592]. For transport-mediated handling, P-glycoprotein (ABCB1) and cytochrome 3A4 drug-drug interactions with targeted therapies raise bioaccumulation risk for DOACs in CTEPH [31113643]. Platelet GTP-bound Rac1, Rap1, RhoA, RalA and Ras were measured to test for a prothrombotic state in CTEPH [25169936, 36984870].

summaries.title: Extracellular matrix organization
summaries.summary: The material frames CTEPH as a disorder of impaired thrombus resolution and vascular remodeling with matrix-related features. Coagulation and fibrinolytic imbalance is prominent: FVIII and VWF antigen are elevated without causative VWF or F8 mutations [41300788], the ADAMTS13–VWF axis is implicated independently of inflammation or disease severity [30655285], plasminogen and alpha2-antiplasmin are reduced while tPA is increased [41300788], low plasminogen with high fibrinogen predicts poor survival [24909805], and t-PA/PAI-1 abnormalities and a PAI-1 polymorphism have been examined [1394930, 41596405]. Endothelial activation and inflammation include ICAM-1 overexpression in endarterectomy-derived endothelial cells, an E469K polymorphism enriched in CTEPH [31324443], and inflammatory cytokine/adhesion molecule production [40567587]. Remodeling involves CD31/α-SMA double-positive intermediate cells in neointima [21854648], altered α-SMA expression in pulmonary artery tissue [22452949], MMP-2 regulation by miR-106b-5p and its inverse relation to collagen-I deposition [32699607, 23738715], TGFβ1 signaling in thrombus nonresolution and fibrosis [31747868, 39274190], raised SPARC [38333700] and osteopontin linked to inflammatory/fibrotic processes and maladaptive RV remodeling [31183846, 37239056], with BMP10 activity falling after pulmonary endarterectomy [39988875] and sGC stimulation modulating endothelial repair [31337550, 36081943].

summaries.title: Gene expression (Transcription)
summaries.summary: This material links CTEPH to inflammation-driven transcriptional programmes rather than to a single transcription factor. NF-κB is activated in CTEPH endothelial cells and in vessels within thrombi (phospho-NF-κB-P65 staining), accounting at least partly for their raised basal pro-inflammatory status [33810533]; PRDX2, increased in patient blood and in rat pulmonary vasculature, limits this NF-κB-dependent inflammation and modulates mitophagy when overexpressed in PAECs, attenuating vascular remodelling, with BAY-11-7085 used to confirm pathway involvement [41372353]. FOXO1, with apoptosis and autophagy, contributes to pulmonary artery remodelling in CTEPH rats [28536427, PPR689684], and EZH2 expression was measured in PASMCs from CTEPH patients [33313943]. Upstream or associated signals include endothelial TGFβ signalling in thrombus nonresolution and fibrosis [31747868, 39274190] and EGFR/ErbB-related circRNA–miRNA networks [28682884, 35053115]. Clonal haematopoiesis is enriched in CTEPH and relates to inflammatory markers and worse prognosis [38116660, PPR661171], while IL-6, CTLA4, adiponectin and PIN1 serve mainly as immune or prognostic markers [41571319, 35572511, 36555549, 29563354, 30942132, 41262940].

summaries.title: Hemostasis
summaries.summary: Within hemostasis, CTEPH is characterised by a procoagulant shift: patients show elevated FVIII and VWF antigen that are not explained by VWF or F8 mutations [41300788], together with reduced ADAMTS13 and increased VWF levels, implicating the ADAMTS13–VWF axis in CTEPH pathobiology independently of pulmonary hypertension severity or systemic inflammation [30655285], although plasma ADAMTS13 is lower in pulmonary arterial hypertension than in CTEPH [34616545]. Extrinsic pathway activation is also implicated, with increased tissue factor antigen and mRNA in monocytes alongside lower plasma TF and higher TFPI, suggesting roles in thrombosis and pulmonary vascular remodelling [26667361, 30942132]. Impaired fibrinolysis is indicated by low plasminogen with high tPA [41300788], low plasminogen predicting poor survival [24909805], and by THBD variants and high TAFI/thrombomodulin expression in pulmonary arteries and thrombus [33103541, 28289017]. Defective thrombus resolution and remodelling involve ANGPT2 [33986029, 36609091], HGF [30594174], SPARC [38333700], reduced NOS3/eNOS [39823269, 37063122], with APOA1 and ALB as biomarkers [33996028, 40941614, 41515551], and FXa (F10) monitoring guiding anticoagulation [39468095, PPR925396].

summaries.title: Immune System
summaries.summary: The material depicts CTEPH as a markedly proinflammatory condition in which innate and adaptive immune mechanisms contribute to thrombus persistence and pulmonary vascular remodeling. Circulating inflammatory mediators are elevated, including CRP, TNF-α and MCP-1 (CCL2), which correlate with plasma tissue factor and are proposed to drive CTEPH thrombosis and remodeling [26667361, 11463608, 32741891]; CXCL10 tracks disease severity and falls after balloon pulmonary angioplasty, and the CXCL10/CXCR3 axis links hemodynamic stress to PASMC hyperproliferation and macrophage-driven perivascular inflammation [35685949, 42017234]. PTX3 was the most sensitive plasma biomarker distinguishing CTEPH from stable pulmonary thromboembolism, while preoperative CRP ≥10 mg/L marks worse functional, hemodynamic and early post-endarterectomy outcomes, and sCD40L has been examined as a surgical-outcome marker, although plasma sCD40L was not increased in CTEPH in one study [25412085, 32007254, 36004182, 15302794]. Adaptive immunity is also engaged: CCR6+ Th17-associated CD4+ T cells are expanded and present in vascular lesions, with altered IFNγ/IL-17 capacity and increased CTLA4 on CD4+ and CD8+ T cells [35572511, 37761997]. Endothelial ICAM1 overexpression sustains the abnormal endothelial phenotype, alongside leukocyte infiltration of endarterectomy specimens, and the RNF213 p.Arg4810Lys variant occurs in a subset of patients, influencing angioplasty response [31324443, 40567587, 39056331, 40240930]; PIN1 levels show sex-specific associations with CTEPH probability and hemodynamics [41262940].

summaries.title: Metabolism
summaries.summary: The material links CTEPH to disturbances in lipid, energy and vasoactive-mediator metabolism. Lipoprotein metabolism is altered: ApoA-I is a more sensitive biomarker than HDL-C and may reflect right heart dysfunction, with concurrent derangements in oxidized dysfunctional oxTrp72-ApoA-I and PON1 enzymatic activity [33996028]. Glycolytic and mitochondrial metabolism is implicated, as PKM2 is elevated in serum and pulmonary endarterectomy tissue of CTEPH patients [39360158], and the PKM2 tetramer may regulate pulmonary artery endothelial cell mitochondrial function via PGC-1alpha and mtTFA, influencing intimal remodeling and pulmonary artery pressure [41811700]. Vasoactive and redox pathways are affected, with decreased eNOS alongside increased HIF-1alpha in CTEPH pulmonary vascular tissue [39823269], downregulated NOS3 with higher pulmonary vascular resistance [37063122], impaired prostacyclin biosynthesis and PTGIS VNTR polymorphisms [15182267], and elevated HMOX1, a candidate drug target [39730379]. Additional metabolic or signalling markers include albumin [40941614, 41515551], adiponectin [29563354, 30942132], H-FABP [18256058, 25412085], HPSE [38333700, 41262940], PIK3CG [41560055] and PIK3R6 [35958401].

summaries.title: Metabolism of RNA
summaries.summary: The material links several RNA-binding and RNA-processing proteins to CTEPH, chiefly through control of glycolytic gene expression. hnRNPA1 regulates glycolysis and proliferative activity by modulating PKM2 expression, and the hnRNPA1/PKM2 axis is proposed as a therapeutic target in CTEPH [39360158]. The related splicing factor PTBP1 acts on PKM2 in a comparable way, indicating that PKM2 is controlled by hnRNP family members (PTBP1 or hnRNPA1) across PH groups [39360158]; a miR-124/PTBP1 axis is hypothesised to shift the PKM2/PKM1 balance and endothelial metabolic programming during progression from pulmonary embolism to CTEPH, contributing to pulmonary arterial intimal remodelling, although these roles remain unclear [40400966]. RNA-export and 3'-end processing factors appear as immune targets or classifiers: autoantibodies against PHAX are higher in CTEPH and PAH patients than healthy donors [30759165], whereas CPSF2 antibodies do not differ by PH status and instead correlate with aortic hypertension [34103026]. PPP1CA was selected by all three algorithms discriminating CTEPH from FM-PH [41827036]. Additional contributors include HSP70 failure supporting endothelial dysfunction and serving as a candidate biomarker [33270690], and Akt-related signalling, with thrombin activating Akt in smooth muscle cells [34736457] and an hsa-miR-122-5p-PIK3CG-PI3K/Akt pathway proposed in CTED deterioration to CTEPH [41560055]; hsa-miR-3148-PRKCA signalling is also suggested as a key CTEPH mechanism [28904974].

summaries.title: Metabolism of proteins
summaries.summary: Protein-level processing and turnover—particularly proteolytic cascades—are repeatedly implicated in CTEPH. Monocyte tissue factor antigen and mRNA are increased while plasma TF is reduced and TFPI raised, suggesting consumption within the extrinsic coagulation pathway [26667361, 30942132], and heparin-calibrated anti-Xa activity has been proposed to guide factor Xa inhibitor therapy [39468095, PPR925396]. Fibrinolytic and VWF-cleaving capacity is impaired, with low plasminogen (alongside low alpha2-antiplasmin and high tPA) predicting poor survival [41300788, 24909805] and decreased ADAMTS13 with increased VWF in CTEPH patients [30655285, 34616545]. Extracellular matrix-modifying proteins are also altered: circulating TGFBI is elevated and falls after pulmonary endarterectomy, marking thrombofibrosis [38362348]; ADAMTSL4 is raised [37448441]; PAPP-A is slightly higher and tracks right ventricular impairment [32746916, 34917333]; and MMP2 is regulated by miR-106b-5p and linked to myocardial collagen deposition [32699607, 23738715]. Additional findings include elevated HIF-1α with reduced eNOS in pulmonary vascular tissue and downregulated HIF1α-AS1 [39823269, 36323673], reduced ApoA-I [33996028], prognostic serum albumin [40941614, 41515551], and a rare MUC6 variant [30047301].

summaries.title: Muscle contraction
summaries.summary: Within the muscle-contraction theme, CTEPH vascular remodelling involves an altered smooth muscle phenotype: α-SMA expression is reduced by about 42% in CTEPH pulmonary artery tissue versus donors, and neointimal cells in proximal pulmonary arteries only rarely co-express the mature contractile markers desmin (DES) and smooth muscle myosin heavy chain (MYH11), unlike medial smooth muscle cells [22452949]; CD31/α-SMA double-positive 'intermediate' cells in distal neointimal lesions suggest endothelial-to-smooth-muscle transition [21854648]. In the hypertrophied right ventricle of CTEPH pigs, the long STIM1 isoform STIM1L is re-expressed while classic STIM1, ORAI1, STIM2, ORAI2/3 and TRPC1/3/4/5/6 proteins are unchanged, and selective ORAI1 inhibition does not alter Ca2+ transients or cell shortening [40248873]. Ion-channel genes are also implicated, with SCN3A upregulated and proposed as a CTEPH marker [35958401, 39727495] and a KCNK3 missense mutation found in one CTEPH patient [26820968, 41072776]. Clinically, atrial stress is reflected by exercise-induced MR-proANP (NPPA) rises marking latent right heart failure [36210266, 33263045], and PDE5 inhibitors are used as vasodilator therapy in inoperable or residual CTEPH [41583269, 33693167]. Annexin A2, a fibrinolytic component, was examined in CTEPH pulmonary arteries to probe microvascular responses [33270690].

summaries.title: Neuronal System
summaries.summary: The material links several genes annotated to this theme with CTEPH, mainly through expression and genetic studies rather than defined neuronal signalling mechanisms. Potassium channel genes feature in two ways: KCNMB2-AS1 showed a downregulated trend in both male and female CTEPH patients relative to controls, suggesting its expression is not sex-specific [35958401], and a missense mutation in KCNK3 exon 1 was found in one CTEPH patient when 7 PAH-causing genes (BMPR2, ACVRL1, ENG, SMAD9, CAV1, KCNK3, CBLN2) were screened in 49 CTEPH patients [26820968]. ERBB4 was elevated in disease groups, allowing 18 GEO CTEPH patients to be stratified into high and low ERBB4 expression groups [39411231], and PRKCA was proposed as an hsa-miR-3148 target in cancer/glioma/ErbB signalling as a possible key CTEPH mechanism [28904974]. GTP-bound Rac1, alongside Rap1, RhoA, RalA and Ras, was measured in platelets of CTEPH, PAH and non-PH patients to test for a prothrombotic condition [25169936, 36984870]. The renin-angiotensin system drove migration of CTEPH PASMCs via ERK1/2 [29122755].

summaries.title: Organelle biogenesis and maintenance
summaries.summary: Within the theme of organelle biogenesis and maintenance, the material centres on mitochondrial biogenesis regulators in CTEPH: the tetrameric form of pyruvate kinase muscle isoform 2 (PKM2) was examined as a regulator of pulmonary artery endothelial cell mitochondrial metabolism acting through PGC-1alpha (PPARGC1A) and mitochondrial transcription factor A (mtTFA/TFAM), thereby influencing arterial intimal remodeling, with lactic acid also implicated [41811700]. Related metabolic regulation is suggested by PPARA, whose agonists reduce TAFIalpha, a contributor to thrombus formation, vascular remodeling and inflammation in CTEPH [40588471], and by implication of the PPAR pathway and CD36 in insulin resistance and fatty-acid metabolism relevant to CTEPH pathogenesis [32110389]. Other listed genes are reported as expression changes or associations rather than defined organelle mechanisms: PAFAH1B1 is upregulated in CTEPH vascular samples [27124368, 33083107]; NOTCH1 expression correlates positively with pulmonary artery wedge pressure in CTEPH [41072776]; ESRRA-regulated genes are upregulated in CD16+ monocytes [39192976]; MEF2D is linked to miR-665-driven smooth muscle cell proliferation and migration [32699607]; and MAPRE1, with PPP1CA, discriminates CTEPH from FM-PH [41827036].

summaries.title: Programmed Cell Death
summaries.summary: The material links CTEPH to apoptosis- and inflammation-related mediators rather than to a single death pathway. Pro-apoptotic signalling is suggested by altered protein levels of FoxO1, Bad and Bcl-2 in a rat CTEPH model [28536427], with increased Bad expression associated with heightened endothelial apoptosis and lung remodelling in rat CTEPH [35732465], while BCL2L1, together with FASN, PLAUR, HMOX1 and RHOB, is proposed to participate in anti-anoikis processes and to serve as a CTEPH diagnostic biomarker [39730379]. Survival signalling is implicated through thrombin-mediated Akt activation in smooth muscle cells [34736457] and a hsa-miR-122-5p–PIK3CG–PI3K/Akt axis in progression from CTED to CTEPH [41560055]. Network analyses place TP53 among the most connected hub proteins, potentially regulated by circ_0007400 as a competing endogenous RNA [36440052], and GSN was defined as a critical interaction module [38333700]. Inflammatory mediators including IL-1β-high macrophages [39192976], IL1B [38451963], HMGB1 [25188497, 36314346] and clonal haematopoiesis [38116660, PPR661171] accompany these changes.

summaries.title: Protein localization
summaries.summary: The supplied material does not describe protein localization mechanisms directly; it instead links these genes to CTEPH through oxidative stress, nitric oxide signalling and cell-type–specific regulatory networks. HMOX1 expression is significantly higher in CTEPH patients than in controls, and targeted drug analysis with molecular docking identified stannsoporfin as a candidate HMOX1-directed therapy [39730379]. Serum oxidative stress markers, including catalase activity, were assessed for prognostic value in PAH and CTEPH but did not differ between the two groups [31929853], although clinical observational studies report that the Cat gene is associated with oxidative stress–mediated pulmonary vascular disease and is significantly downregulated in PAH and CTEPH [35237384]. APP is proposed to act in a circ_0026692/circ_0021630–miR-20b-5p–APP axis in fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells, endothelial cells and myofibroblasts, and is among the most highly connected nodes in cell-type protein–protein interaction networks [36440052]. For NOS2-related signalling, strategies include riociguat, PDE5 inhibitors, and stabilizing NOS or supplying L-arginine to restore NO production [28895506]. No mechanistic role is given for ACOT8, whose citation concerns endothelin-1–targeted therapy and shared microvasculopathy between CTEPH and iPAH [39550495].

summaries.title: Reproduction
summaries.summary: The material links five genes annotated to this theme with CTEPH, although it describes vascular, haemostatic and haematopoietic observations rather than reproductive processes themselves. Rare variants in SOX17, alongside RASA1, ENG, GDF2, ACVRL1 and RNF213, were found exclusively in CTEPH patients and not in pulmonary embolism patients without CTEPH, and SOX17, known from primary pulmonary hypertension (type 7), is considered a plausible CTEPH candidate [41300788]. In expression profiling, SOX17 and TET2 levels correlated negatively with systolic pulmonary artery pressure in IPAH, with CTEPH showing a distinct gene and miRNA profile in which NOTCH1 correlated with pulmonary artery wedge pressure [41072776]. Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential mutations are enriched in CTEPH, most commonly affecting DNMT3A, RUN1 and STAG2 [PPR661171]. Podoplanin (PDPN) and other vessel-specific genes were expressed at lower levels in white CTEPH thrombi than in organizing venous or aortic aneurysm thrombi [24526692]. Serum DIDO1 autoantibody levels did not differ between CTEPH patients and healthy donors [34103026].

summaries.title: Sensory Perception
summaries.summary: The material assembled under the Sensory Perception theme does not describe sensory signalling itself in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH); instead it links the listed genes to plasma biomarkers, transcriptomic markers and network modules. Plasma ApoA-I, together with HDL-C, paraoxonase-1 activity and oxidised dysfunctional oxTrp72-ApoA-I, was compared between CTEPH patients and healthy controls, with ApoA-I judged a more sensitive biomarker than HDL-C and possibly associated with right heart dysfunction [33996028]. Transcriptomic analyses report upregulation of the sodium voltage-gated channel alpha subunit 3 (SCN3A) in CTEPH patients [39727495] and propose SCN3A, alongside LINC00472, PIK3R6 and TCL6, as potential gene markers, in analyses enriched for chemokine signalling, metabolic pathways, arachidonic acid metabolism and MAPK signalling [35958401]. Network analysis identified gelsolin (GSN), with HPSE and SPARC, as a significant interaction module potentially relevant to CTEPH pathogenesis [38333700]. A miRNA-target analysis suggested hsa-miR-3148–PRKCA acting through cancer/glioma/ErbB signalling as a possible key mechanism [28904974], while TTR appears only indirectly, as prealbumin among nutritional markers proposed for prognostic evaluation [40422933].

summaries.title: Signal Transduction
summaries.summary: Signal transduction via vasoactive, chemokine and growth-factor receptor pathways is repeatedly implicated in CTEPH. Endothelin-1 signalling, studied together with TGF-β, is proposed to drive microvasculopathy and vascular remodelling, and circulating ET-1 was measured before and after pulmonary endarterectomy, although preclinical evidence for ET-1 receptor antagonism in CTEPH remains limited [39550495, 39274190]. Chemokine signalling is prominent: CXCL10 is elevated and falls after balloon pulmonary angioplasty [35685949], and the CXCL10/CXCR3 axis links haemodynamic stress to remodelling through PASMC hyperproliferation and macrophage-driven inflammation [42017234]; CXCL13 is overexpressed in vascular lesions [26927848, 33947407], CXCL9 may recruit cytotoxic lymphocytes, NK cells and macrophages and predict prognosis [33947407, 37761997], CCR6+ Th17-associated T cells are increased [35572511], and TNF and CCL2 correlate with tissue factor and remodelling [32741891, 26667361, 11463608]. Endothelial signalling is altered, with decreased NOS3 alongside increased HIF-1α [39823269, 37063122], elevated VWF/FVIII unexplained by VWF mutations [30655285, 41300788], raised serum HGF [30594174], Pin1 elevation in men [41262940], and rare BMPR2 variants [24728306, 32397294].

summaries.title: Transport of small molecules
summaries.summary: Within the theme of transport of small molecules, the material links CTEPH to altered coagulation initiation, lipid transport, carrier proteins and ion handling. Monocyte tissue factor antigen and mRNA are increased in CTEPH, with plasma TF reduced and TFPI raised, suggesting extrinsic-pathway activation contributes to thrombosis and pulmonary vascular remodelling [26667361, 30942132]. Lipid-transport markers are also affected: ApoA-I (including oxidised oxTrp72-ApoA-I) is a more sensitive biomarker than HDL-C and may reflect right heart dysfunction [33996028], while Lp(a) encoded by LPA is significantly higher in CTEPH than in PPH or controls [9716143]. Serum albumin inversely correlates with length of stay and predicts prolonged hospitalisation and mortality [40941614, 41515551], and copeptin (AVP-derived) is altered in CTEPH and falls after therapy [33263045, 26363916]; NGAL/LCN2 elevation associates with poor prognosis [33122779]. Ion- and solute-transport genes implicated include ANO1 polymorphisms and methylation with serum chloride [42346503], RYR2 nanostructure with unchanged TRPC1/TRPC6 in right ventricle [40248873], SLC2A3 [33316641, 34957234] and HMOX1 [39730379].

summaries.title: Vesicle-mediated transport
summaries.summary: The material frames CTEPH largely through secreted and circulating mediators rather than intracellular trafficking per se. Procoagulant secretion is prominent: monocyte TF antigen and mRNA are increased while plasma TF is lower and TFPI higher, implicating the extrinsic pathway [26667361, 30942132], and FVIII with vWF:Ag are elevated, suggesting endothelial activation [36890726, 41300788]. Released alarmin and matrix proteins are also altered, with raised serum HMGB1 [25188497, 36314346] and higher plasma SPARC than in IPAH, PTE or controls [38333700]. Growth-factor signalling shows increased systemic EGF with reduced serum EGFR [35053115], and an ErbB-linked circRNA–miR-940–CRKL axis has been proposed [28682884]. Plasma and immune markers carry prognostic weight: ApoA-I relates to right heart dysfunction [33996028], albumin predicts hospitalisation and mortality [40941614, 41515551], haptoglobin is higher than in PAH [29069014], soluble CD163 predicts poor outcome [33122779], CCR6+ CD4+ T cells are expanded [35572511], and copeptin falls after therapy [33263045, 26363916].

summaries.title: Methods of the genetic studies of CTEPH
summaries.summary:
**Designs over time.** The earliest CTEPH genetics was dominated by candidate-gene association studies of haemostatic variants and by single-patient reports [8883290, 10706510, 11454828, 11555695, 11796466]. From the mid-2000s HLA typing and microsatellite mapping of the HLA region appeared [15640334, 18931448, 19165231, 21930318], followed by pharmacogenetic genotype-stratified treatment analyses [24531084, 26821322]. After 2015 the field moved to targeted next-generation sequencing panels of pulmonary arterial hypertension and thrombophilia genes [26820968, 32397294, 36338413, 41300788], whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing with family/linkage designs [27122457, 30047301, 40221599, 40726512], clonal-haematopoiesis/somatic analyses [38116660, 39604025], and finally GWAS and Mendelian randomisation [38470220, 41163636, 41915478, 42877973].

**Populations.** Japanese cohorts were prominent early, covering PTGIS VNTR, ACE I/D and HLA studies [15182267, 16936432, 15640334, 18931448, 19165231, 21930318] and later exome screening [33103541]. Other East Asian work used Han Chinese cohorts for FGA variants, PAH-gene panels, pedigree WGS and CTEPH GWAS [23894515, 26820968, 40221599, 42877973]. European, German, Swiss, Turkish, Czech and US cohorts followed [32397294, 19844076, 36856592, 39150410, 40726512]; population ancestry was frequently unstated.

**Sample sizes and controls.** Cases ranged from single patients to nearly 2000 [34317315, 41163636], with a median near 51. Controls were heterogeneous: healthy volunteers [18057060, 36856592, 42346503], other pulmonary hypertension or post-embolism patients without PH [10706510, 17287300, 20182352, 26820968, 41300788], surgical lung specimens [31324443], or public databases such as gnomAD, ToMMo, 3.5KJPN and UK Biobank [32397294, 33103541, 39604025, 40726512].

**Platforms and quality control.** Methods spanned PCR/RFLP and TaqMan or FRET real-time PCR [10706510, 23894515, 36856592, 39150410, 41596405, 42346503], MassARRAY genotyping [30047301], Sanger sequencing [36338413], and Illumina exome/panel/genome sequencing with BWA, GATK, MuTect2, ANNOVAR and ACMG/HGVS classification, CADD and in-silico prediction filters, depth and variant-allele-frequency thresholds, and Hardy–Weinberg checks [33103541, 39604025, 40221599, 40726512, 41300788]. GWAS used four arrays, ancestry principal components and Haplotype Reference Consortium imputation [38470220].

**Statistics and limits.** Most studies compared genotype and allele frequencies by chi-square/Fisher tests with odds ratios and logistic regression [18057060, 23894515, 36338413, 39150410], occasionally adjusting for haemodynamics, age or sex [16936432, 26821322, 39604025]. Formal multiple-testing correction (Pc, Holm, Benjamini–Hochberg, genome-wide thresholds) was used only in some studies [19165231, 33103541, 38470220, 41163636], and explicit replication was rare [27122457, 38470220, 40221599, 40726512]. Limits recurring in the material include unreported ancestry, small or absent control groups, non-healthy comparison groups, abstract-only method reporting, and lack of hemodynamic confirmation of CTEPH [41596405].

summaries.title: Findings of the genetic studies of CTEPH
summaries.summary:
**Replicated associations.** Fibrinogen genes are the most consistently implicated: the FGA Thr312Ala variant was associated with CTEPH in three independent case–control studies [18057060, 23894515, 36856592], and an FGA 3'UTR Ins/Del allele (modulated by miR-759) in another [20677013]; FGG was identified at genome-wide level in two studies [38470220, 42877973]. Coagulation loci ABO [38470220, 39150410, 42877973], F11 [38470220, 39150410], F2 [38470220, 39150410] and F5 [38470220, 20182352] were each associated in two studies, together with MYH7B, TSPAN15, SLC44A2 and HLA-DRA [38470220]. Other single-study associations include ICAM1 E469K [31324443], SERPINE1 4G/5G [41596405], STAB2 rare variant enrichment [40726512], CLEC7A, TNFSF13B, LRP1, ETS1 and FGR by Mendelian randomisation [41915478], and CTSS by multiomic prioritisation [42877973]. GNB3 C825T [24531084, 26821322] and ACE genotype [16936432, 26821322] were associated with outcome/clinical worsening rather than susceptibility.

**Population-specific findings.** In Japanese cohorts, HLA-B*5201 and HLA-DPB1*0202 were more frequent in patients [15640334], the association being confined to deep-vein-thrombosis-negative CTEPH, together with NFKBIL1 IKBL-p*03 [19165231]; HLA-B*5201 status also stratified clinical phenotype, thrombus distribution and surgical outcome [18931448, 21930318]. ACE D-allele carriage predicted lower walk distance and survival in Japanese patients [16936432]. Chinese studies reported ACVRL1 c.1450C>G, enrichment of nonsynonymous variants in BMPR2/ACVRL1/ENG/SMAD9/CAV1/KCNK3/CBLN2 and the SNPs rs3739817 and rs55805125 [26820968], PROC/PROS1/SERPINC1 variants in thrombophilic patients [36338413], and novel GP6, TET2 and JAK2 variants in families [40221599].

**Acquired/clonal variants.** JAK2 V617F was repeatedly reported in CTEPH with myeloproliferative neoplasms [33024690, 35381612, 36949868, 42698555] and was enriched as a pathogenic variant in one cohort [32397294]. Clonal haematopoiesis mutations (DNMT3A, TET2, RUNX1, ASXL1) occurred in 9.4% of patients [38116660], and CH-associated variants in 20.1%, rising to 44.4% at age 80–89 [39604025].

**Negative candidates.** Factor V Leiden and prothrombin G20210A were not associated in several series [8883290, 10706510, 11555695, 25796019, 36338413, 41596405]; likewise PTGIS [15182267], BMPR2 [17287300, 41300788], NOS3 and HTR2A [19844076], OR2T3 [27122457], VKORC1/CYP2C9 [36856592], MTHFR and F13A1 V34L [41596405], ANO1 [42346503], and CPB2, FGA, VWF/F8 in one sequencing study [41300788].

**Strength of evidence.** Evidence is strongest for coagulation/fibrinogen loci (replicated GWAS) and Japanese HLA associations; most other genes rest on single studies, small samples or case reports, and thrombophilia findings are inconsistent [41300788, 11454828, 41063787, 41425438].
